blocks.text: In all the aqueous solutions, the concentration of H⁺ and OH⁻ are too low to be conveniently expressed and used in calculations. In 1909, Sorenson, a Danish biochemist, introduced the term pH and pOH. So, the scales of pH and pOH were developed. These two quantities can be calculated as:

blocks.title: Interesting Information!
blocks.text: Solutions of negative pH and having values more than 14 are also known.
The value of pH normally varies between 0 → 14 at 25 °C.
The pH values of some familiar aqueous solutions are shown in Figure 9.1. This table can help you to understand the acidic or basic nature of commonly used solutions.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The pH gives the H⁺ concentration, not OH⁻: [H⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ = 10⁻⁹·² ≈ 6.3 × 10⁻¹⁰ M. The OH⁻ concentration comes from the pOH: [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁴·⁸ ≈ 1.6 × 10⁻⁵ M.

The ionic product of water at a certain temperature is Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 25 ºC. If the concentration of H⁺ ions in a solution is 1.0 × 10⁻⁷M. Calculate the concentration of OH⁻ ions, the pH and pOH of the solution.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ / 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷, so [OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ M; this is the value used for pOH = 7.

blocks.prompt: a) A solution is prepared by mixing equal volumes of two solutions: one with a pH of 4.0 and another with a pH of 10.0. Calculate the Kw for this mixture at 25°C.
blocks.explanation: Kw depends only on temperature, not on the solution. At 25°C, Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ for this mixture too. (The pH 4.0 solution has [H⁺] = 10⁻⁴ M and the pH 10.0 solution has [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁴ M; in equal volumes they neutralize each other, so the pH of the mixture is about 7.)

blocks.prompt: b) At a specific temperature, the ionic product of water Kw is 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴. If the concentration of OH⁻ ions in a solution is 2.5×10⁻⁸ M. Calculate the concentration of H⁺ ions and the pH of the solution.
c) Copper-plate etching solutions is prepared by diluting concentrated HNO₃ to 0.30 M HNO₃. Calculate [H⁺], pH, [OH⁻] and pOH of this solutions at 25 ºC.
blocks.explanation:
HNO₃ is a strong acid and ionizes completely, so [H⁺] = 0.30 mol dm⁻³.
pH = −log 0.30 = 0.52
[OH⁻] = Kw / [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ / 0.30 = 3.3 × 10⁻¹⁴ mol dm⁻³
pOH = 14 − 0.52 = 13.48
